title: Computer Networks

concepts.title: Architectures and Design Principles
concepts.brief: Establish the intellectual framework for the book: layered abstraction, end-to-end arguments, modularity, control/data-plane separation, and the economics of network design. Cover: layering, cross-layer design, and where layering breaks down; end-to-end principle, fate sharing, and protocol design trade-offs; control plane, data plane, and management plane; performance, scalability, reliability, and complexity as competing objectives; case study: why the Internet architecture evolved as it did.

concepts.title: Packet Processing and Forwarding Systems
concepts.brief: Examine what actually happens inside modern switches and routers, beyond the abstract "forward a packet" model. Cover: packet parsing, classification, lookup, and scheduling; longest-prefix matching, TCAMs, algorithmic route lookup, and hashing; switch fabrics, buffering, head-of-line blocking, and cut-through versus store-and-forward; programmable data planes: P4, programmable ASICs, SmartNICs, and DPUs; high-speed implementation constraints: memory, power, timing, and deterministic behavior.

concepts.title: Routing: Algorithms, Protocols, and Policy
concepts.brief: Treat routing as both an algorithmic problem and a policy-driven system, rather than as a catalog of protocol commands. Cover: distance-vector, path-vector, and link-state approaches; OSPF, IS-IS, BGP, route reflection, and route redistribution; BGP policy, route selection, route leaks, hijacks, and RPKI; convergence, stability, route oscillation, and scaling limits; Segment Routing, MPLS, and traffic-engineering-oriented routing.

concepts.title: Transport Beyond TCP Basics
concepts.brief: Focus on the mechanisms that make transport protocols robust at Internet scale, including congestion behavior, latency, and modern transport design. Cover: TCP state machines, loss recovery, reordering, and path MTU discovery; congestion-control families: loss-based, delay-based, rate-based, and learning-based; CUBIC, BBR, DCTCP, QUIC congestion control, and fairness implications; QUIC architecture: streams, encryption, connection migration, and 0-RTT trade-offs; multipath transport, MPTCP, and transport for data-center and wireless networks.

concepts.title: Congestion, Scheduling, and Quality of Service
concepts.brief: Analyze how networks allocate scarce resources under contention and how QoS mechanisms interact with real traffic. Cover: queueing models, buffering, delay, jitter, and loss; active queue management: RED, CoDel, FQ-CoDel, and ECN; scheduling disciplines: FIFO, WFQ, DRR, and hierarchical scheduling; DiffServ, IntServ, RSVP, MPLS traffic engineering, and their deployment realities; QoS for interactive, real-time, and high-throughput workloads.

concepts.title: Network Security and Trust
concepts.brief: Move beyond "add a firewall" toward security as a property of protocols, infrastructure, and operational practice. Cover: threat models: on-path attackers, BGP hijacking, DNS abuse, and insider threats; TLS, IPsec, DNSSEC, SSH, and authenticated key exchange; firewalls, NAT, proxies, zero-trust access, and microsegmentation; DDoS defense, rate limiting, anomaly detection, and scrubbing; supply-chain, configuration, and operational security risks.

concepts.title: Software-Defined Networking and Programmability
concepts.brief: Explain SDN as an architectural shift, not merely a controller product, and connect it to programmable forwarding. Cover: separation of control and data planes; northbound and southbound interfaces; OpenFlow, P4, gRPC/gNMI, NETCONF/YANG, and intent-based networking; controller placement, consistency, failure handling, and scale-out control planes; network programmability, verification, and automated configuration; use cases: data-center fabric control, WAN traffic engineering, and telemetry-driven operations.

concepts.title: Virtualization, Overlays, and Cloud Networking
concepts.brief: Show how virtual networks are constructed, isolated, and operated across shared physical infrastructure. Cover: VLANs, VXLAN, GRE, GENEVE, and overlay-underlay interaction; network virtualization, multi-tenancy, and isolation boundaries; virtual switches, service chaining, NFV, and eBPF-based data-plane functions; cloud networking: VPCs, load balancers, gateways, private connectivity, and hybrid networks; performance isolation, troubleshooting overlays, and multi-cloud design patterns.

concepts.title: Wireless, Mobile, and Edge Networks
concepts.brief: Address networks where capacity, mobility, interference, and energy constraints dominate design decisions. Cover: wireless fundamentals: spectrum, interference, link adaptation, and MIMO; Wi-Fi evolution, cellular architectures, 5G, and network slicing; mobility management, handover, roaming, and mobile IP concepts; edge computing, latency-sensitive applications, and local breakout; IoT, LPWAN, satellite networking, and constrained-device protocols.

concepts.title: Measurement, Operations, and Future Networks
concepts.brief: Close with the skills needed to understand, diagnose, and evolve production networks. Cover: telemetry, flow monitoring, active probing, and observability pipelines; SLAs, SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, and failure analysis; network verification, digital twins, intent validation, and AIOps; emerging directions: quantum networking, post-quantum security, AI-native networking, and space networks; capstone case studies: hyperscale data center, global CDN, enterprise zero-trust network, and 5G edge deployment.

images.prompt: A technical drafting plate: white and cyan line art on deep navy, thin uniform strokes, orthographic or exploded-cutaway construction, dimension lines and leader arrows over a faint grid. A schematic, not a picture — no shading, no dramatic perspective. Subject: an exploded cutaway of the Internet as an engineering drawing — on the left a laptop and a phone, in the middle a chain of routers and a data-center switch rack drawn in exploded view so their line cards and switching fabric show, on the right a distant server farm; links between them drawn as thin lines, one wireless link drawn as concentric arcs, and a single packet's route traced in a slightly brighter cyan with leader arrows calling out each hop. Faint stacked layer planes float behind the drawing like transparent sheets of tracing paper. Generous whitespace, no text labels baked in. Target size ~1280×720px, 16:9 landscape; compose for a cover figure with the subject centred and safe margins — it is letterboxed into a 16:9 box, so keep nothing important near the edges.
images.alt: A drafting-plate drawing of a network: hosts, routers and switches joined by links, with one packet's path traced in the accent line
images.caption: One packet's trip, drawn as a set of plans.

summary: An expert tour of network architecture, protocol internals, and operations — from forwarding hardware and BGP policy to QUIC, SDN, overlays, wireless, and measurement — told in plain words with a picture for every idea.
